analysis.summary: A survey of fuzzing for database management systems, arguing that DBMSs differ from general-purpose software in internal structure, input and output, and testing objectives, so they need strategies that existing fuzzing surveys do not cover. It defines a general fuzzing procedure, decomposes existing methods against it, and classifies them again by testing objective across DBMS components. It also presents an open-source toolkit, OpenDBFuzz, and uses it to compare the surveyed methods experimentally.
